note: E1-E6 follow-up experiments from cross-model analysis. E1 and E3 are the highest-impact findings.

e1_fullcontext_anchoring_ablation.question: Does the full-context 'brooding intellectual' pattern come from temporal anchoring or text volume?
e1_fullcontext_anchoring_ablation.verdict: NOT temporal anchoring. Shuffled full-context reproduces the same polarization as ordered (N+8.9, E-4.0 vs ordered N+6.9, E-5.0). The mechanism is text volume, not recency/primacy.
e1_fullcontext_anchoring_ablation.secondary_finding: First-quarter is closest to the chunked baseline (deltas against the private reference profile are withheld). Last-quarter shows higher E (37.0 vs 30.0). The biographical reading of that shift is withheld: it is an inference about a private individual's life, not a temporal-slicing result.

e2_o_facet_falsification.question: Is O stability a ceiling artifact or genuine trait stability?
e2_o_facet_falsification.verdict: PARTIALLY FALSIFIED. O domain stability is driven primarily by O5_Ideas at ceiling (range 7.5 across registers). O4_Actions varies 28.2 points. Domain-level compression is an aggregation artifact of one dominant facet, not uniform stability.

e3_narrative_2x2_replication.question: Do the A (-11.7) and C (-13.8) generator effects survive replication?
e3_narrative_2x2_replication.verdict: GENERATOR EFFECTS ARE NOISE. Original A delta was -11.7, replicated is +2.1. Original C delta was -13.8, replicated is +1.5. The single-run Opus-gen scores (A=55.7, C=69.0) were outliers. Under replication, both generators produce nearly identical profiles when read by Opus.

e4_facet_analysis.top_finding: C2_Order drops 41.5 points in GPT-gen narrative (Opus-eval). But E3 replication suggests this may also be noise from a single-run outlier.

e6_emotional_density.verdict: NOT SUPPORTED. Emotional content intensity does not predict GPT E inflation.

e5_debiased_prompt.verdict: MITIGATED. Debiased prompt nearly eliminates full-context polarization. N shift reduced from +6.9 to +0.2, E from -5.0 to -1.0, O from +2.7 to -1.1, C from +2.4 to -0.3. All domains return to within ~1 pt of chunked baseline. The 'brooding intellectual' pattern is a prompt-addressable attentional anchoring effect.
e5_debiased_prompt.note: Prompt appended: 'weight mundane/neutral passages as heavily as emotionally intense passages. Do not anchor on the most salient or dramatic moments.'

e3_replicated_2x2.note: UPDATED with full replication (2-3 runs per cell, all 4 cells complete)
e3_replicated_2x2.verdict: GENERATOR EFFECT CONFIRMED NEGLIGIBLE. Mean 1.8 pts (unchanged from original). EVALUATOR EFFECT MUCH LARGER THAN ORIGINALLY ESTIMATED: 12.4 pts (vs original 5.6). The original 3x ratio was depressed by single-run outliers in one cell; true ratio is ~7x.

implications_for_existing_claims.generation_confound_is_small: CONFIRMED AND STRENGTHENED. Generator effect = 1.8 pts under replication, consistent across evaluators. The original 'large A/C generator effects' (11.7 and 13.8 pts) were single-run outliers that collapsed to <2 pts under replication.
implications_for_existing_claims.evaluator_dominates_generator: DRAMATICALLY STRENGTHENED. Ratio is 6.8x (not 3x). Evaluator effects of 12.4 pts mean vs generator effects of 1.8 pts. E (+16 pts) and A (+17 pts) are the largest evaluator-dependent domains.
implications_for_existing_claims.full_context_anchoring: CLARIFIED AND FIXABLE. The effect is about text volume, not temporal order (shuffling doesn't help). But a debiased prompt ('weight mundane passages equally') almost fully mitigates it, returning all domains to within ~1 pt of chunked baseline.
implications_for_existing_claims.original_single_run_data_unreliable: The Opus-gen/Opus-eval single run had A=55.7 and C=69.0 — both >12 pts above replicated means. Posts citing these specific numbers need correction.
